questions.q: Why is hardcoding a server name directly into a script a problem?
options: It turns the script into a single-use artifact that only ever works against that one server, instead of a reusable tool
PowerShell scripts cannot technically contain string literals
It causes a syntax error
It is actually best practice for production scripts
questions.explain: A param() block with variables (and sensible defaults) makes the same script reusable across any server or database instead of copy-pasted and hand-edited each time.

options: It enables -WhatIf/-Confirm support on the function, but doesn't by itself prevent anything — you still need a $PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess() call around the destructive action
It automatically deletes files matching a filter
It permanently disables the function
It has no effect unless combined with Remove-Item specifically
questions.explain: SupportsShouldProcess just makes the -WhatIf/-Confirm parameters available; the actual gating happens at the $PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess() call around the risky line.

options: Long, hard-to-read parameter lists — parameters are collected into a hashtable and passed with @ instead of listed inline with $
It makes a script run faster at the CPU level
It automatically validates parameter types
It replaces the need for a param() block entirely
questions.explain: Splatting is purely a readability and maintainability pattern for calls with many parameters — each one gets its own line in a hashtable.

questions.q: Running a properly -WhatIf-enabled function with -WhatIf against production should do what?
options: Print what the operation would do (e.g. "What if: Performing the operation...") without actually performing the destructive action
Perform the action immediately, then print a warning afterward
Silently do nothing with no output at all
Throw an unhandled exception every time
questions.explain: That's the entire point of -WhatIf — a safe preview of exactly what the script would touch, without touching it.

questions.q: In the lesson's combined example (Backup-DbaDatabaseSafely), which three patterns are used together?
options: A param() block for inputs, SupportsShouldProcess/ShouldProcess for safety, and a splatted hashtable for the actual Backup-DbaDatabase call
Only splatting, nothing else
A GUI form, a try/catch block, and a scheduled task
Hardcoded values, no error handling, and inline parameters
questions.explain: The function combines all three patterns from the lesson: parameterized inputs, a ShouldProcess safety gate, and splatting for the underlying dbatools call.
